question: What is the primary role of the registered nurse in team nursing?
explanation: The registered nurse acts as the team leader who coordinates and delegates tasks to other members. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T4#GNS123_U1_T4_h1)

question: Why was the team nursing model originally introduced into healthcare systems?

options.A: To eliminate the need for shift handovers
options.B: To replace doctors in rural clinics
options.C: To address severe shortages of professional nurses
options.D: To increase the cost of hospital admissions

explanation: Post-war nursing shortages necessitated a model that utilized fewer professional nurses supported by auxiliary staff. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T4#GNS123_U1_T4_h1)

question: A core goal of team nursing is achieving efficient use of skills by doing what?

options.A: Giving all tasks exclusively to nursing students
options.B: Matching specific tasks to appropriate training levels
options.C: Assigning doctors to perform basic hygiene care
options.D: Rotating every staff member through surgery daily

explanation: Tasks are distributed based on each worker's legal scope of practice and clinical competence. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T4#GNS123_U1_T4_h2)

question: How does team nursing support junior staff members and students?

options.A: By providing direct mentorship from experienced nurses
options.B: By removing all supervision during procedures
options.C: By making them solely responsible for ward management
options.D: By isolating them from clinical decision making

explanation: Working closely within a structured team allows junior staff to learn clinical skills safely under supervision. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T4#GNS123_U1_T4_h2)

question: Who holds ultimate legal accountability for the care plan in team nursing?
explanation: The registered nurse team leader retains overall responsibility for assessing and evaluating patient care plans. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T4#GNS123_U1_T4_h3)

question: What is an appropriate duty to delegate to auxiliary health workers?

options.D: Measuring and recording routine vital signs

explanation: Auxiliary staff are trained to handle basic supportive tasks like measuring vital signs and assisting with hygiene. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T4#GNS123_U1_T4_h3)

question: What is the primary purpose of the daily team nursing conference?

options.A: Conducting formal disciplinary hearings for staff
options.B: Discussing patient status and updating care plans
options.C: Reviewing the monthly hospital financial budget
options.D: Planning social events for the ward personnel

explanation: The conference ensures all team members are aligned on patient needs and daily assignments. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T4#GNS123_U1_T4_h4)

question: What negative outcome occurs most often when team communication breaks down?

options.A: The ward receives more medical supplies
options.B: Patients automatically pay lower hospital bills
options.C: Care becomes fragmented and clinical details are missed
options.D: Doctors take over all bedside nursing duties

explanation: Poor communication stops vital patient information from reaching the right staff members, leading to gaps in safety. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T4#GNS123_U1_T4_h4)

question: Which of the following is a major advantage of team nursing?

options.C: Guaranteed private rooms for all patients
options.D: Cost-effective use of mixed skill sets

explanation: The model appropriately distributes tasks among professionals and auxiliary staff to optimize resources. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T4#GNS123_U1_T4_h5)

question: Why might continuity of care suffer under the team nursing model?

options.A: Doctors refuse to communicate with the nursing team
options.B: Patients receive care from multiple different staff members
options.C: Care plans are never written down on paper
options.D: Wards operate without any registered nurses present

explanation: Because tasks are divided among various team members, a patient may interact with several different nurses daily. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T4#GNS123_U1_T4_h5)

question: How does primary nursing differ fundamentally from team nursing?

options.A: Doctors directly assign hourly chores to orderlies
options.B: One nurse maintains 24-hour accountability for a specific patient
options.C: Auxiliary workers manage all clinical medications alone
options.D: Only nursing students are allowed to make care plans

explanation: Primary nursing gives a single nurse continuous responsibility for a patient throughout their hospital stay. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T4#GNS123_U1_T4_h6)

question: What is the main operational difference between total patient care and team nursing?

options.A: Team nursing eliminates the need for patient documentation
options.B: Team nursing requires no registered nurses on duty at any time
options.C: Total patient care assigns all care to one nurse, whereas team nursing divides tasks among a group
options.D: Total patient care is only used in outpatient clinics

explanation: Total patient care involves a single nurse doing everything for the patient, while team nursing utilizes a hierarchical group. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T4#GNS123_U1_T4_h6)

question: What major staffing issue often disrupts team nursing in Nigerian hospitals?

options.A: High patient-to-nurse ratios and chronic staff shortages
options.B: Too many doctors performing bedside nursing duties
options.C: An excess of registered nurses in every ward
options.D: The complete absence of auxiliary healthcare workers

explanation: Severe staff shortages make it difficult to maintain proper team structures and supervision on busy wards. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T4#GNS123_U1_T4_h7)

question: A team leader notices friction between junior nurses and auxiliary staff over duties. What is the best immediate action?

options.A: Report all staff members immediately to the hospital board
options.B: Clarify roles and scopes of practice during a brief team meeting
options.C: Stop all delegation and do every single task alone
options.D: Ignore the tension as it will resolve itself over time

explanation: Clear communication and reinforcement of legal scopes of practice resolve role confusion and reduce workplace friction. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T4#GNS123_U1_T4_h7)
